answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the new release, against a daily settlement peak that historically held when headroom was already in place (b3). That makes the release the novel factor, not load alone. Prior rollback restored a stable build without dropping customer writes (b1)—need the archive to confirm that analog still fits latency rather than only error spikes. Circuit breakers are rejected: failing fast would sacrifice customer writes (b4), which violates the objective. Failover and read-replica routing lack a regional or report-query signal. One intervention, so roll the release back rather than test capacity. Uncertainty remains because peak write volume is concurrent.
